To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the economic crisis of 2008/09 was the worst since the Great Depression of the 1930s.
the economic growth of the world economy has been very slow since the financial crisis, and that the growth of the world’s economy is expected to be even slower in the coming decade.
the global economic crisis has been a severe and prolonged recession, but that it is now in its final stages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the extent to which South Africa is integrated into the international economy.
the relationship between economic growth, income inequality and poverty in the context of the South African economy.
the question of how the world economy will evolve in the next few years, and how South Africa’s economy can benefit from this.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no clear-cut answer to the question of what caused the Great Recession and the subsequent recovery.
the South African economic performance in 2009 was disappointing, but that the economy is now on a sounder footing, and that prospects for the future are better.
the global economy has recovered from the 2008-9 crisis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the global economy is still struggling to find a way out of the Great Recession.
the global financial crisis was a crisis in the financial system, not the real economy, and that the policy response was to save the financial system, which was successful.
the global financial crisis has been overcome and we are back to business as usual.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global economic recovery was driven by a surge in government spending, especially in advanced economies.
the recovery in emerging economies has been much more robust than in advanced economies, and that the gap between the two has continued to widen.
, despite some differences, the overall pattern of recovery in the world economy was remarkably similar across countries.
